title: Kyber Achieves HIPAA Compliance, Strengthening Data Security for P&C Insurers
summary: The milestone reinforces Kyber's commitment to protecting sensitive information and supporting secure, governed insurance correspondence workflows.
body_markdown:
**NEW YORK, NY, November 5, 2026** – Kyber, an AI-native correspondence management platform built for property and casualty (P&C) insurers, today announced that it has achieved compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). This milestone marks another step in Kyber's continued investment in data security, privacy, and enterprise governance.


Insurance correspondence can involve sensitive personal, financial, and medical information, particularly in claims workflows. As insurers evaluate technology to support these communications, data security, privacy, and governance remain important considerations.


Kyber's HIPAA compliance reflects its continued investment in the safeguards and security practices needed to support workflows involving sensitive information.


‍


## Supporting Secure Insurance Correspondence


HIPAA establishes requirements for protecting the privacy and security of protected health information (PHI). Kyber's compliance milestone reinforces its commitment to responsible data handling and maintaining appropriate safeguards for sensitive information.


For P&C insurers, this milestone provides additional assurance as they evaluate the security and compliance capabilities of the technology supporting their operations.


"Insurance carriers trust us to support critical communications, and protecting the information behind those workflows is a responsibility we take seriously," said Arvind Sontha, Founder and CEO of Kyber. "Achieving HIPAA compliance is an important milestone as we continue building the secure, reliable infrastructure insurers need to manage correspondence at scale."


‍


## Built for Enterprise Security and Governance


Kyber's HIPAA compliance builds on its SOC 2 Type II attestation, reflecting its continued investment in enterprise security, data protection, and governance.


Beyond these security milestones, Kyber continues to invest in the capabilities insurers need to manage correspondence securely and with greater control.


The platform brings document generation, template management, review and approval workflows, and delivery into one connected platform. Capabilities such as role-based permissions, configurable approvals, and audit trails help insurers maintain visibility and oversight throughout the correspondence lifecycle.


By connecting these workflows, Kyber helps claims and operations teams reduce manual work while maintaining greater control over how communications are created, reviewed, and delivered.


To learn more about Kyber and its correspondence management platform, visit[www.askkyber.com](http://www.askkyber.com/) .


‍


### About HIPAA


The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) is a U.S. federal law that establishes standards for protecting the privacy and security of certain health information. Its implementing regulations require covered entities and business associates, as applicable, to implement safeguards for protected health information (PHI). The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through its Office for Civil Rights (OCR), enforces the HIPAA Privacy, Security, and Breach Notification Rules.


‍


### About Kyber


Kyber is an AI-native correspondence management platform built for P&C insurers. By connecting claims data, document generation, template management, and correspondence workflows, Kyber helps insurers automate correspondence, reduce manual work, and manage communications with greater control.
